issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a method named printFarmSong(), but both the template and the solution implement and reference a method named singFarmSong(). This naming mismatch can confuse students about which method to implement and what the tests expect (the Main template also calls singFarmSong()).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement and UML to refer to singFarmSong() everywhere, or (B) rename the public method in the template and solution from singFarmSong() to printFarmSong(), and update all references in Main and comments accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement requests implementation of a method named printFarmSong() in Farm.java, but both the template and the solution define and use singFarmSong() (and singFarmSongVerse()). This mismatch between the method name in the specification and the actual code can confuse students about which method to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Either update problem_statement.md to ask for singFarmSong() (and singFarmSongVerse()) instead of printFarmSong(), or rename the method in the template and solution from singFarmSong() to printFarmSong() (and update any calls in Main.java) so the specification and code match.
